matches.why: All thirteen state the same mechanism as P-01: GET /invoices/:id binds req.params.id but the SELECT has no owner_id predicate, so any caller reads any invoice; nearly all contrast it with the safe /receipts/:id which does add AND owner_id = $2. R20 and R36 also mention missing authentication, but both explicitly name the absent ownership check on the same query, so they are this defect. Rejected near-misses in the same file: R52 ('Missing Authentication Middleware Enforcement') whose stated mechanism is that no middleware sets req.user on /receipts, /invoices and /payments - a different failure (unauthenticated access) than an authenticated caller reading another tenant's row; and R77 ('Missing Authentication on /branding/preview Endpoint'), a different route and again about authentication, not object scoping. R10 belongs to neither, it is about /payments SQL.
matches.quote: Line 8: `SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE id = $1` queries only by invoice id without filtering by owner.

matches.why: All seventeen describe req.query.order being string-interpolated into `ORDER BY ${order}` in GET /invoices, noting that a bind parameter cannot stand in for a column. R16 (line 19), R72 (line 16), R79 (line 20), R80 (line 17) and R59 (lines 20-23) misplace the line number but quote the same /invoices statement, so they still are this defect. Rejected near-miss in the same file: R10, 'Incomplete SQL Injection Mitigation in /payments Endpoint', which targets the SAFE counterpart - /payments maps req.query.sort through the SORTABLE allowlist before interpolating - and only speculates that a future careless edit could reintroduce injection; that is a different (and currently non-existent) mechanism, not P-02.
matches.quote: The order parameter from the query string is interpolated directly into the SQL query using template literals, without parameterization or allowlist validation.

matches.why: All eighteen describe the one defect P-03 spans across two files: POST /branding/preview passes req.body.logoUrl straight to fetchLogo(), which calls fetch(url, {redirect:'follow'}) with no allowlist, while fetchAsset() next to it parses the URL, checks ALLOWED and uses redirect:'error'. Findings filed at either location count (R31 and R62 name both files; R83, R34, R58 and R65 emphasise the redirect-following half). R34 is titled 'Open Redirect / Unvalidated Redirect' but its stated mechanism is fetchLogo's redirect:'follow' letting the server be steered to internal addresses - that is the same defect, not a separate open-redirect bug. Rejected near-miss on the same route: R77, 'Missing Authentication on /branding/preview Endpoint', whose mechanism is the absence of an auth check on the handler, not the unvalidated outbound fetch; it would remain true even if fetchLogo were fully allowlisted.
matches.quote: The fetchLogo(url) function at lib/remote.js:5-8 accepts any URL and fetches it via node-fetch without validation.

matches.why: All seventeen state that lib/auth.js calls jwt.decode() (line 6 in currentUser, line 12 in tagRequest) instead of jwt.verify(), so the signature is never checked and the sub/role claims that decide identity are attacker-controlled. R32, R50, R71, R48 and R75 shift the line number (4, 5, 12) but quote the same jwt.decode call. Rejected near-misses in the same file and the same functions: R12, 'Undefined Return Value in tagRequest Function', whose mechanism is that tagRequest returns req.session.user which no code ever sets - a correctness bug about the return value, not about signature verification; and R85, 'Weak JWT Parsing Allows Null User Context', whose mechanism is that a MISSING or malformed token yields {id: undefined, role: undefined} that may slip past a falsy check downstream - the opposite failure from a well-formed forged token being trusted.
matches.quote: Line 6: `const claims = jwt.decode(bearer);` uses jwt.decode() which does not verify the signature.

matches.why:
All fifteen name the same sink: invoiceNote() interpolates the customer note into `
${note}
` with no escaping, while customerName() in the same module escapes with escapeHtml() and footer() coerces with Number(). Labels vary (reflected, stored, HTML injection) and severities range from medium to high, but the mechanism stated is identical - unescaped interpolation at the HTML sink - so the varying labels do not split them. R49 (line 3), R09/R25/R45/R51/R56/R69 (line 4) and the rest (line 5) all point at the same three-line function. No near-miss was rejected here: no finding in lib/render.js targets customerName() or footer().
matches.quote: The `note` parameter is interpolated directly into an HTML string without escaping.
